newsitem.title: USA: Lawmakers welcome Fed decision on interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Lawmakers welcome Fed decision on interest rates.

text.p: Democratic and Republican lawmakers welcomed the Federal Reserve's decision on Tuesday to hold interest rates steady, but that did not stop them from criticizing the central bank on other grounds.
"The Fed's decision is a sigh of relief for America's families but it's hardly cause for celebration," Democratic Sen. Tom Harkin from Iowa said.
"The real debate at the ... Federal Reserve shouldn't be about raising interest rates -- it should be about lowering them," Harkin, a frequent Fed critic, added in a statement.
Rep. Henry Gonzalez, a Texas Democrat, agreed.

"The Fed should roll back the last interest rate increase to let the American public know they are not fighting economic growth," Gonzalez, the ranking Democrat on the House Banking Committee, said in a separate statement.
The central bank in March raised interest rates for the first time in more than two years, bumping up the key federal funds rate by a quarter percentage point.
"We also agree with today's decision to keep rates unchanged," said Rep. Jim Saxton, Chairman of the Congressional Joint Economic Committee.
But the New Jersey Republican said the Fed needs to explain why it chose to leave rates steady on Tuesday.
"This is just as important as providing rationale for an actual policy change," Saxton said. "Such information helps markets work better by removing uncertainties."
In a statement, he called for an earlier release of both edited and verbatim minutes of Federal Open Market Committee meetings.
The edited version of the minutes is now released with a lag of about six weeks. The verbatim transcript is released after five years.
